A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MobileIPL research, with the same core framework and three benchmarks. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original MobileIPL evaluations on AITZ, AMEX, and AndroidControl, alongside ablations, sampling analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original benchmark evaluations and reports additional GRPO comparisons, instruction-evolution and reward ablations, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The specified click reward changes from the distance-threshold formulation in v1 Equation 7 to a type-gated, normalized-distance formulation in v3 Equations 7–8. These expressions are not equivalent as printed. The CoaT stages, sampling, backward credit assignment, preference filtering, and iterative DPO framework remain intact; the PDFs do not establish that implementation or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use AITZ, AMEX, and AndroidControl, including long-trajectory tasks and unseen-app/unseen-task evaluation. The new comparisons and ablations operate within retained coverage. Shortening the dataset descriptions in v3 does not establish removal of tasks or action types.

E2.justification: v3 adds Qwen2-VL-7B trained with GRPO to AndroidControl Tables 3–4. It removes the plain CogAgent and AUTO-GUI rows from Table 1 while retaining their CoaT variants, and removes Claude* and GPT-4o from Table 3. The remaining benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Table 5 changes the IPL-removal comparison from a sixth-round MobileIPL reference to a first-round reference. v3 also introduces a stated equal-compute GRPO comparison and an experiment substituting BERT similarity for the F1 reward. The common learning rates, resolutions, batch size, context length, epochs, and AndroidControl subsampling in Appendix D remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially revises the component-analysis evidence: Table 5 directly removes instruction evolution while retaining IPL, replacing the earlier nested SFT/evolution/dialogue/history ablations. Appendix C adds an F1-versus-BERT reward test, and Appendix G adds computational-cost analysis across iterations. The detailed CLICK/PRESS sampling-count analysis and pie charts from v1 Appendix F are removed, although the main scaling plot and annotation case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-training-run counts, training random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing embedding-dispersion statistics and Figure 3 deviation display are retained. References to a seed model concern initialization for IPL, not statistical replication.

E6.justification: Headline MobileIPL scores remain 69.15 on AITZ, 74.29 on AMEX, and 72.7 AndroidControl Step.Acc. Added results include GRPO's 69.8 Step.Acc in Table 3, first-round performance without evolution of 62.9 versus 65.4 in Table 5, and F1/BERT total accuracies of 65.37/62.49 in Table 8. Table 9 adds sample counts and training times. Several baseline and ablation entries disappear, PRESS sampling proportions are revised, and the naive-DPO deficit annotation is corrected from −4.1 to −5.1.

T1.justification: The reward definition is substantively revised, while the tree-value recursion, sampling-space definitions, and seed-selection mathematics are retained. For a type-correct, nonexact click, v3 Equations 7–8 imply a reward of (1 + vtype + vformat)(1 − d), which can exceed the stated upper bound of 1 for small nonzero distances. No new theorem or proof resolves this inconsistency.

C1.justification: The conclusion now explicitly claims that instruction evolution generates more IPL training data and thereby improves IPL performance. v1 emphasized increased output diversity and negligible direct downstream improvement. The principal claims about the framework, benchmark superiority, and out-of-domain generalization remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explains evolution's benefit through additional preference data and recasts PRESS recovery around early underrepresentation. It adds an exact-keyword-matching rationale for F1 rewards. More consequentially, it removes v1's limitations concerning lengthy sampling and potentially biased baseline reproduction, while the new cost discussion characterizes IPL overhead as modest. The earlier explicit grounding disadvantage is also dropped from the main discussion, although the underlying scores and annotation-ambiguity cases remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a dataset-access link, a reproducibility statement, and per-round training sample counts and times in Table 9. Most implementation settings and prompts are retained. The explicit v1 sentence about stopping at a test-set performance bottleneck disappears; v3 discusses convergence without identifying an alternative evaluation set. These documentation changes do not establish changed experimental execution.

R1.justification: The reference list retains the same works, and the main positioning against GUI pretraining and preference-learning approaches remains stable. Section 3.2 newly attributes the advanced FAQ design to inspiration from Shen et al. (Falcon-UI), adding a limited relationship to an already cited work.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. v3 retitles the paper, standardizes multi-turn terminology, and rewrites selected method, results, ablation, and interpretation paragraphs. It moves ethics into the main text, adds a reproducibility statement, and reorganizes the closing appendices, including an LLM-usage statement.

P2.justification: v3 broadly changes the document template and float arrangement: Tables 1–4 are consolidated onto one page, figures are resized or relocated, and headings and table spacing change throughout. It restructures Table 5, adds Tables 8–9, and removes the original Figure 4 pie charts. The main analytical graphics and case-study figures are retained, with the later appendix figures renumbered.

improvement.justification: The direct evolution ablation, GRPO comparison, and reward-design test strengthen the empirical support. However, v3 removes material reproduction limitations and calls compute overhead modest despite Table 9 reporting IPL round times totaling 13.6 hours versus 2.8 hours for SFT. Its revised click reward can also violate the stated reward range, without clarifying which formulation produced the unchanged main results. These substantive benefits and unresolved harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
